title: Naturality of the base-change comparison with the relative Mayer–Vietoris triangles
statement: Let X' \xrightarrow{g'} X and S' \xrightarrow{g} S form a cartesian square, let f:X\to S be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and let f':X'\to S' be its base change [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-base-change]. Assume moreover that S and S' are affine. Let K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X) and K'\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{X'}) be objects, together with a morphism L(g')^*K\to K' in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{X'}) [def-pc-derived-category]. If X=U\cup V with U and V quasi-compact open subschemes and U\cap V quasi-compact, write U'=X'\times_X U and V'=X'\times_X V, and put W'=X'\times_X W for W in {X,U,V,U\cap V}. For each such W, let \alpha_W be the composite Lg^*R(f|_W)_*(K|_W)\to R(f'|_{W'})_*L(g'|_{W'})^*(K|_W)\to R(f'|_{W'})_*(K'|_{W'}) of the derived base-change morphism for f|_W [def-pc-derived-base-change-map] and R(f'|_{W'})_* of the restriction to W' of the given morphism, using derived pullback and direct image [def-pc-derived-pullback, def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Apply Lg^*Rf_* to the derived Mayer--Vietoris triangle of K for the cover X=U\cup V, and Rf'_* to that of K' for the cover X'=U'\cup V' [lem-pc-derived-mayer-vietoris-triangle], identifying Rf_*R(j_W)_* with R(f|_W)_* and Rf'_*R(j_{W'})_* with R(f'|_{W'})_*. Between the two resulting distinguished triangles in D(\mathcal O_{S'}), the maps \alpha_X, \alpha_U\oplus\alpha_V, and \alpha_{U\cap V} form a morphism of distinguished triangles.

proof.text: Since S and S' are affine, g is affine [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], hence so is its base change g', and g' is quasi-compact and separated [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. Since f is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and S is affine, X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine]; likewise f', the base change of f, is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (Tags 01K5 and 01KU, elementary), so X' is quasi-compact and quasi-separated over the affine S' [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine]. As g' is quasi-compact, U'=(g')^{-1}(U), V'=(g')^{-1}(V) and U'\cap V'=(g')^{-1}(U\cap V) are quasi-compact opens with X'=U'\cup V'. Hence the derived Mayer--Vietoris node applies to K on X=U\cup V and to K' on X'=U'\cup V' [lem-pc-derived-mayer-vietoris-triangle]. Applying the exact functors Lg^*Rf_* and Rf'_* gives distinguished triangles in D(\mathcal O_{S'}). For each W in \{X,U,V,U\cap V\}, the canonical composition isomorphism Rf_*R(j_W)_*\cong R(f|_W)_* (and its primed analogue) identifies the terms with the objects used to define \alpha_W [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-composition].

source.place: Tag 0DJ9, induction step; apply the relative Mayer--Vietoris triangles and identify composites of derived direct images

proof.text: Let \psi:K\to Rg'_*K' be the adjoint of the given morphism L(g')^*K\to K' under L(g')^*\dashv Rg'_* [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general]; Rg'_*K' lies in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X) because g' is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-preserves-qcoh]. Since restriction to opens commutes with these adjunctions, \psi|_W corresponds to the restricted morphism L(g'|_{W'})^*(K|_W)\to K'|_{W'} under (Rg'_*K')|_W\cong R(g'|_{W'})_*(K'|_{W'}). By the definition of the base-change morphism [def-pc-derived-base-change-map] (the unit of L(g')^*\dashv Rg'_* followed by naturality of the unit), the adjoint of \alpha_W under Lg^*\dashv Rg_* is Rf_*R(j_W)_*(\psi|_W) followed by the composition isomorphisms Rf_*R(j_W)_*R(g'|_{W'})_*\cong Rf_*Rg'_*R(j_{W'})_*\cong Rg_*Rf'_*R(j_{W'})_* [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-composition]. By part (1) of [lem-pc-derived-mayer-vietoris-functorial] applied to \psi, the maps \psi, R(j_U)_*(\psi|_U)\oplus R(j_V)_*(\psi|_V), R(j_{UV})_*(\psi|_{U\cap V}) form a morphism of distinguished triangles MV(K)\to MV(Rg'_*K'), connecting square included; by part (2) with h=g' (X' qcqs and U', V' quasi-compact by Step 1), MV(Rg'_*K')\cong Rg'_*MV(K') as distinguished triangles, compatibly with the connecting morphisms. Applying the triangulated functor Rf_* and the composition isomorphism Rf_*Rg'_*\cong Rg_*Rf'_*, the adjoints of \alpha_X, \alpha_U\oplus\alpha_V, \alpha_{U\cap V} form a morphism of distinguished triangles Rf_*MV(K)\to Rg_*Rf'_*MV(K'). The adjunction bijection \mathrm{Hom}(Lg^*A,B)\cong\mathrm{Hom}(A,Rg_*B) is natural in A and B and compatible with the shift isomorphisms of the triangulated functors Lg^* and Rg_*, so each of the three squares (the connecting square alpha_X[1]\circ Lg^*Rf_*(\delta)=Rf'_*(\delta')\circ\alpha_{U\cap V} included) commutes because its adjoint square does. Hence (\alpha_X,\alpha_U\oplus\alpha_V,\alpha_{U\cap V}) is a morphism of distinguished triangles.
